lessons.title: Beating Disguise
lessons.blurb: What the offense does about it.

steps.title: Make them declare
steps.body: Motion before the snap forces the defense to adjust: a defender who travels says man; a rotation of safeties says zone. Shifts do the same with whole formations.

steps.title: Tempo
steps.body: Snapping fast leaves no time to rotate, walk down or sub. A defense that has to line up quickly usually shows what it plays.

steps.title: Bunch and stack
steps.body: Receivers lined up close together make man defenders fight through traffic and force zone defenders to pass routes off, both of which expose a disguise.

steps.title: Alerts
steps.body: Some plays carry an alert: if the middle of the field opens after the snap, throw the post; if it closes, work the play underneath. The quarterback reads the post-snap safeties, not the pre-snap ones.

steps.prompt: The defense keeps rotating late. What's the simplest offensive answer?
choices: Go tempo so they can't disguise
steps.explanation: Without time to disguise, defenses tend to play what they show.

steps.prompt: After the snap, the middle of the field opens up. What does an 'alert' tell the quarterback?
steps.explanation: An open middle after the snap is the alert to take the post.

steps.statement: Stack and bunch formations make man coverage easier to play.
steps.explanation: Receivers close together create rubs and traffic, which makes man coverage harder.
